title: Integrated Learnware Identification and Reuse via Reusability-Aware Metric Learning

problem.claim: Learnware systems need to identify existing models that can benefit new user tasks through reuse.

gap.claim: Identification based only on training-distribution or task similarity may not reflect performance after reuse.

contributions.claim: The system uses reuse experience among hosted learnwares to make specifications characterize reusability for new user tasks.
The system treats hosted learnwares as pseudo-user tasks and evaluates the performance of identifying and reusing other learnwares for them.
The system evolves specifications into a reusability-aware space in which shorter distances indicate higher expected reuse performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments demonstrate that reusability-aware identification can effectively recommend learnwares that benefit new user tasks after reuse.

narrative_sequence.summary: The learnware paradigm reuses trained models to help users solve machine learning tasks.
A learnware dock stores models with capability specifications and identifies models whose training distributions align with user tasks.
Task similarity alone may not predict whether an identified learnware performs well after reuse.
Reuse evaluations among hosted learnwares guide the evolution of specifications into a reusability-aware metric space.
The authors report that reusability-aware identification effectively recommends learnwares benefiting new user tasks.

source_observation.claim: The system uses prior cross-learnware reuse performance to reshape specifications and guide future identification.

interpretation.claim: Retrieval representations can be improved by incorporating downstream reuse outcomes rather than relying only on input or task similarity.

application.claim: For reusable-model repositories, train or calibrate retrieval metrics using observed performance of retrieved models on representative tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach works when reuse histories are sparse, unrepresentative, or unavailable.

unknowns: Datasets, task domains, baselines, metrics, and quantitative experimental results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the metric-learning objective, optimization procedure, or deployment requirements.
The abstract does not report limitations or the conditions under which reuse-history-based identification may fail.
